_README: Surveyed ground control points, one entry per camera.
Fill lat/lon for each point from satellite imagery (Google Earth, or
Bhuvan at bhuvanmaps.nrsc.gov.in), then run:
python -m backend.scripts.solve_gcp_calibration CAM_08
which reports the leave-one-out error, and --promote to write it.
RULES that decide whether this works:
1. Every point must be ON THE GROUND. A homography maps a single plane,
so a rooftop, a sign, or the top of a pole will corrupt the fit. Use
the point where a pole MEETS the road, not the pole.
2. Spread the points across the area vehicles are tracked in. Points
clustered in one corner leave the rest of the frame unconstrained.
3. At least 5 points. Four determine the homography exactly, so with
only four the measured error is zero by construction and tells you
nothing. The 5th and beyond are what make the number real.
4. Use 6-7 decimal places of lat/lon. Four decimals is ~11 m and would
dominate the error you are trying to measure.
5. Permanent features only, never a parked vehicle or a market stall.
6. Prefer CORNERS and INTERSECTIONS over points along a line. A spot
partway down a kerb is ambiguous from above; the corner where two
kerbs meet is not.
HOW ACCURATE DOES EACH READING HAVE TO BE? Measured by simulating this
solver on a synthetic junction, 25 trials per cell, worst leave-one-out
error in metres, with 1.5 px of click error on the image side:
satellite err   5 pts   6 pts   8 pts   10 pts
gate: good < 0.50 m | degraded <= 1.00 m | else rejected
So aim for TEN points read to about 0.10 m. Five points cannot reach
'good' at any precision — there are not enough of them to average the
reading error down.

independent_check.description: IRC:35 zebra stripes are 500 mm wide with 500 mm gaps, so consecutive stripe centres are 1.000 m apart across the road. Measured on a 90-frame median of CAM_08_0830.mp4: stripe pitch is 50.00 px (std 1.84) along the crossing axis. Any homography solved from these GCPs must reproduce ~1.0 m there. The calibration active on 2026-09-09 returned 1.61-5.44 m, i.e. ~3x wrong.
